notes.l0: L0 needs no rule. It is the default outcome when the Answer supports a proposition, the pinned snapshot records no equivalent support for the candidate, and neither an active scoped rule nor a proof applies. L0 is an observation about one snapshot under the Open World Assumption.
notes.l1: L1 requires an ACTIVE rule with a declared scope. A different observed object alone is never L1.
notes.l2: L2 requires a machine-checkable proof carrying premises, a conclusion and an ontology or schema source. The l2_rules list below is EMPTY for the Journal-2 pilot: DBpedia infobox properties (the dbp: namespace) carry no functional, maximum-cardinality, disjointness or negative-assertion declarations, and none is available offline. Declaring one here would fabricate exclusion evidence. Zero L2 cases in the pilot is therefore the correct reported outcome, not a gap to be filled.
notes.temporal_l2: Temporal L2 additionally requires real statement-level qualifiers. DBpedia infobox facts have none, so qualifier_status is UNAVAILABLE_IN_SOURCE and temporal L2 is unreachable on this source by construction.
notes.okuhara_inference_templates: Okuhara 2025 uses P(x,y) AND P(y,z) -> P(x,z) and P(x,y) AND capital(z,y) -> P(x,z) to add panoramic bypass links. Those are link-creation heuristics, not negative-evidence rules and not statement qualifiers, and they are deliberately NOT used as L2 exclusion rules here.

empirical_single_valued_derivation.scope_note: The scope is the Answer plus the complete ranked candidate pool of the Prompt-8C selected class, as serialized by Prompt 8D. It is a LOCAL, EMPIRICAL scope: the rule says nothing about the predicate outside this class and nothing about DBpedia as a whole.
empirical_single_valued_derivation.minimum_support_note: Support is the number of distinct entities in the scope observed with at least one object for the key. Five is the declared default; the run sweeps 3, 5, 8 and 10 and publishes the sensitivity in empirical_rule_candidates_v3.csv, so the threshold is auditable rather than silent.
empirical_single_valued_derivation.violation_note: A violation is an entity in scope observed with two or more CANONICALLY DISTINCT objects for the key. Canonical equivalence is applied first, so a redirect pair does not count as two values.
empirical_single_valued_derivation.inactive_direction_note: For an IN key the observed cardinality is an IN-DEGREE: how many other articles in the local pool happen to point at the entity with that predicate. A maximum in-degree of one across a handful of entities reflects how thinly the snapshot covers those articles, not a property of the predicate. IN-direction candidates are therefore derived and published as PROPOSED_NOT_ACTIVE so the ablation can show exactly what they would change.

l1_rules_note: Curated L1 rules would be listed here. The pilot declares none: every L1 rule it uses is DERIVED at run time by empirical_single_valued_derivation above, from the frozen Prompt-8D observations, and is published with its support, maximum observed cardinality, violation count and activation status in empirical_rule_candidates_v3.csv.

functional_conflict_requirements: a trusted functional or maximum-cardinality declaration from ontology_source
an observed alternative object on the candidate
canonical inequality between the Answer object and the candidate object
no equivalence and no parent-child support relation between them
temporal_conflict_requirements: actual statement-level qualifiers on both statements
l2_rule_schema.non_functional_predicates_note: birthPlace, almaMater, knownFor, influenced, author, products and similar predicates are NOT treated as functional merely because one value happens to be observed for one entity.
